decisions.reason: As a low-risk burner component tied to the installed radiant-heating base, it likely stays because even if its results are only modest the firm has enough growth and slack to retain such an incremental complement.

This electric infrared panel line remains a strategic flagship in the shift toward lower-carbon solutions, so management would be inclined to keep it and continue learning unless performance clearly fell far below aspirations.

The electric halogen infrared heater is the least central and most exposed to pruning if it underperforms relative to other new lines, but the firm's breadth, growth and tolerance for experimentation still make continuation slightly more likely than withdrawal.

Because this industrial electric infrared hall-heater line fits core customer applications and supports the firm's system-selling logic, management would usually keep it while demand and positioning become clearer.

The hydrogen-capable dark-radiant line is highly aligned with the firm's future direction and already had real-operation validation, so any shortfall would more likely trigger refinement than discontinuation.
